sections.h2: India imported ₹239.49 crore of diamond powder in 2024–25 and exported ₹27.45 crore

chart.title: Imports of diamond powder outweigh exports by about ₹212 crore a year
chart.sub: ₹ crore, HS 710510 (diamond dust and powder), FY 2024–25.

sections.means: Net of exports, India's diamond powder bill is a deficit of about ₹212 crore in one year.
sections.todo: Track the powder deficit as a supply-security line, not as a sign of diamond-industry strength.

sections.h2: India's lab-grown output would cover about 1% of its powder imports by carats

chart.title: Lab-grown output is roughly 1% of the powder India imports
chart.sub: Million carats. Lab-grown output is this blog's estimate from reported yields.
chart.source: Indian Bureau of Mines; this blog's estimate.

sections.means: Grinding up every lab-grown stone the industry grows would cover only about 1% of the powder bill by weight.
sections.todo: Build HPHT grit capacity rather than rely on lab-grown gem growing to replace imported powder.

sections.h2: China's licence on fine diamond powder is suspended only until 10 November 2026

chart.title: The licensing rule is paused, not cancelled, and its suspension ends 10 November 2026
events: Announcement No. 55 puts synthetic diamond micropowder under export licensing, due to take effect 8 November
Announcement No. 70 suspends the licensing rule with other export controls
Suspension ends unless extended; a licence is not a ban

sections.means: A Chinese export licence on the powder behind most of India's diamond polishing is on a timer.
sections.todo: Plan for India to have no domestic fallback at scale if the suspension lapses.
